clue.text: Don't insinuate foolishly it has more than 200 members

indicators.note: acting foolishly suggests the letters of the first two words are jumbled senselessly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is being told not to make sly hints about a large organisation's size.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, leaving thirteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The world body has well over a hundred and ninety member states, and counting observers and agencies the setter rounds it generously.

clue.text: Legendary one, woman who joined Velvet Underground, cremated?

indicators.note: the question mark asks what happens to the cremated singer: she ends up inside the vessel

parts.note: a cremated person's ashes go in an urn
Nico was the German singer who joined the Velvet Underground on their first album

explanation.surface: A question about a famous singer's funeral: was she cremated?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cremated?' both supplies the urn and says the singer goes inside it, so the question mark flags a cryptic leap rather than a straight synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-horned horse is a creature of myth, a legendary beast.

clue.text: Place to spend the night having sex — know what I mean?

parts.note: an inn offers rooms for overnight guests
'it' is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside about a hotel stay with a nudge and a wink.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang tag question, from 'isn't it', is used by speakers seeking agreement, much like 'you get me?'

clue.text: Nationalist party overwhelmed by Irish support

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so the first pieces sit inside the word for Irish

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A political party of nationalists is swamped by Irish voters' backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or product is to give them one's public approval, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Company without ownership is something extraordinary

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a firm that belongs to no one
from the idiom 'like ...', meaning remarkably or to an extraordinary degree

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is an unowned firm; idiomatically, doing something 'like' this means doing it exceptionally.

clue.text: It may cover the roof of the little church over there

parts.note: 'that' points at something at a distance, as in 'that one over there'
CH is the short form of church

explanation.surface: Pointing out the straw roof of a small chapel in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid as a roof covering is a traditional roofing material in English villages.

clue.text: Preventing old boy replacing leader of aircraft industry

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes the place of the first letter of the industry word

parts.note: aviation is the business of building and flying aircraft
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil takes over at the top of an aerospace company.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of AVIATION (the leader of 'aircraft') gives way to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obviating a problem means forestalling it, so the noun is the act of averting something.

clue.text: Tips for a clue writer? Tell!

parts.note: read as a clue, the two-word phrase would be 'spit' with 'out' as an anagram signal, giving the word tips

explanation.surface: Advice for someone who writes puzzle clues, followed by an order to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue writer could clue the word 'tips' as SPIT OUT, since 'out' signals a rearrangement of SPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit something out is to say it at last, so the imperative urges someone to speak up.

clue.text: Fellow in Norway? No!

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a Scandinavian man is Norwegian and is corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: this Nordic man is from the country next door, not Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a Nordic neighbour often mistaken for a Norwegian by outsiders.

clue.text: French writer about to leave goodbye message after rejecting English plot

indicators.note: the farewell piece comes after the turned piece
rejecting something turns it back, so the plot and its English label are read backwards

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: the word for about is taken out of the farewell

parts.note: au revoir is French for goodbye
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A French author bids farewell after turning down an English storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns E BED into DEBE; 'to leave' takes RE out of AU REVOIR, leaving AUVOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone de Beauvoir was the French existentialist author of The Second Sex.

clue.text: Liam Fox, for one, defined by day and month Remain lost

indicators.note: the verb meaning remain goes missing from the month's name

parts.note: October is a month
to be is to remain or exist

explanation.surface: A Brexit-backing politician is linked to an exit date when the Remain side lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Fox is a British Conservative politician and Brexiteer who trained as a GP; October 2019 was a Brexit deadline. BE leaves OCTOBER to give OCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Before entering Parliament the MP worked as a general practitioner, so he is an example of a medical man.

clue.text: John Thomas Murphy said to be one like Stalin

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the slang pair is heard as the answer

parts.note: John Thomas and Dick are both slang for the penis, and Murphy and tater are slang for a potato, giving dick tater

explanation.surface: A man's full name, with the claim that he resembles a Soviet leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is not a person but two pieces of British slang: 'John Thomas' (a penis, a dick) and 'Murphy' (a potato, a tater).
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin ruled with absolute power, the very model of an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Being simple-minded when always wanting sun instead of cold? Not at all

indicators.note: every occurrence of the cold letter has to want, so both are swapped, not just one
the sun letter goes in where the cold letter was

parts.note: innocence is naivety, being guileless or simple-minded

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about someone naive who always wants sunshine instead of cold.
explanation.walkthrough: INNOCENCE has two Cs; 'always' means both become S.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverbial phrase means in no way or by no reckoning, a firm denial.

clue.text: Immediately beyond control

definitions.meaning: to reject something ... is to do so at once, without thought
a situation that gets ... is no longer manageable

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom serves both as 'without hesitation' and as 'unmanageable', two distinct senses.

clue.text: In hindsight, time to remove obscene stuff …

indicators.note: hindsight looks back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: to rid is to remove or clear away

explanation.surface: Looking back, it is time to clear away filthy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut and filth are slang for indecent material, as in 'dishing the dirt'.

clue.text: … with which this elder statesman could become the one at No 11

indicators.note: the letters of the two words together could be rearranged into the other entry

parts.note: the answer to the clue numbered 11 in this puzzle, a word for a tyrant
refers back to the previous clue's answer, the filth

explanation.surface: A sequel clue suggesting a statesman could become someone living at Number 11 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 11' looks like Downing Street, the British Chancellor's residence; it is the 11-across answer. Its letters are this answer plus 14-across's.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman famed for his stern moral censorship.

clue.text: Composer's heartsick, partly upset after breaking up?

indicators.note: only part of the compound, the sick half, is turned over while the heart half stays put

parts.note: split as heart and sick: the core is the heart of something, and ill means sick
the second half of heartsick, sick, gives ill
ill turned upside down, as the indicator asks

explanation.surface: A composer is heartbroken after a split with a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after breaking up?' hints that heartsick must be broken into its two halves before the second is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer of concerti grossi.

clue.text: Sea horses adopting awful sound

indicators.note: the horses take in the other piece, holding it between them

parts.note: two horses: H is slang for heroin, known as horse, and a bay is a reddish-brown horse

indicators.note: something awful is messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seahorses taking in a dreadful noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea horses' looks like the marine creature; the first word is the definition, and the horses are heroin (H, slang 'horse') and a bay horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The large inland sea in northern Canada is named after the explorer Henry Hudson.

clue.text: S Club 7

parts.note: a putter is a golf club, and it has seven letters

explanation.surface: The name of a British pop group of the late 1990s.
explanation.walkthrough: S Club 7 were a British pop group. Read as S plus a seven-letter club, it gives S PUTTER; the setter jokes that their singing is a splutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke casts the pop act's singing as spluttering, an unkind description of their sound.

clue.text: Records in unchanged clean condition

indicators.note: the records go inside the phrase meaning unchanged

parts.note: as is means in its present state, unchanged
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Old vinyl records kept pristine and untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term is the absence of germs, a sterile state as in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Rock climbing mostly safe here in California

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Gib is short for Gibraltar, known as the Rock

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: sure means safe, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: Rock climbing being reasonably safe at a spot in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses GIB into BIG; 'mostly' trims SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugged stretch of coast in central California is a famous scenic region along Highway 1.

clue.text: It's written on the wall: "old tennis star, well-trained one"

parts.note: Steffi Graf is a retired German tennis champion
fit means in good trained condition
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wall slogan praising a former tennis champion as well trained.
explanation.definitionFit: Spray-painted words and drawings on public walls are the classic example of street scrawl.

clue.text: US government expels a thousand moneylenders

indicators.note: throwing out means the two pieces are removed from the name

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the US government
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Washington throws out a thousand loan sharks.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against pledged goods.

clue.text: Maize removed from Goat Island

indicators.note: the grain word is taken away from the star sign

parts.note: Capricorn is the zodiac sign of the goat
corn is maize

explanation.surface: Maize crops have been cleared from a place called Goat Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat Island' looks like one name, but Goat is the star sign and Island the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian isle in the Bay of Naples is a well-known holiday resort.

clue.text: No score against Chelsea playing with ten

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are put into play and moved about

explanation.surface: A football team kept a shutout while Chelsea were down to ten men.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a team keeps a shutout when it concedes no goals in a match.

clue.text: Very good headers from Sergio Agüero for City

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious, very good

indicators.note: the initial letters, the heads, of the two names are taken

explanation.surface: Praise for goals headed by Manchester City striker Sergio Agüero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' wants to be Manchester City, Agüero's club; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city is famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Having difficulties like Mark Knopfler once

definitions.meaning: to be in a very tight situation, in trouble
Mark Knopfler was guitarist and singer of the rock band Dire Straits

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in serious trouble is also the literal state of a member of Knopfler's old band.
